context: ˆ We note that the effective Lindbladian Le [Eq. (6)] can in general contain higher-order operators than the operators in the Hamiltonian or the dissipative jump ˆ operators. This is because the effective Lindbladian Le is calculated by taking the logarithm of the noise channel that evolves the system from the beginning to the end of the protocol. As shown in Eq. (3), this noise channel is the time-ordered exponentiation of the usual Lindbladian as defined in Eq. (2). The time-ordered exponentiation can be expressed using the Magnus expansion [49, 50] as the exponentiation of infinite series of operators evaluated from nested commutators involving each term in the Hamiltonian and dissipative jump operators. Since some of the Hamiltonian and dissipation terms do not commute, the commutators give rise to higher-body operators in the noise channel which then translates into higher-body operators in the effective ˆe Lindbladian L. For our example of the 3-qubit processor, the effective Lindbladian contains correlated qubit jump operators, i.e., two- or three-body jump operators, resulting from the commutator of the qubit-qubit couplings in Eq. (20) and the individual qubit jump operators in Eq. (22). Moreover, it also comprises three-qubit coupling terms, arising from the commutator between two neighboring two-qubit coupling terms in Eq. (20).
